ActivityCategory.description:
Activity is an intentionally separate projection. Adding a field to the
security audit does not automatically expose that field in product feeds.

ApplicationIdentity.description:
A concrete application identity used by traffic rules. A display name is
deliberately not part of the identity: it is presentation-only and cannot
authorize or select a route.

CapabilityKind.description:
The fixed first-version capability set. Unknown wire values fail closed at
deserialization and are never inferred from a free-form label.

oneOf.description:
A migrated record may preserve an unreadable state without making the
capability usable. New writes may not create this state.

path.description: Unambiguous JSON Pointer rooted at the configuration document.

ConfigurationDocument.description: Complete, redacted configuration document returned to every UI adapter.

networks.description: Network name to complete TOML-equivalent JSON object.

oneOf.description: The running data plane consumes this change without a process restart.
Persisted now; the affected network process must restart to consume it.

ConfirmedTrafficDirectFallback.description:
Explicit, acknowledged permission to fall back to the operating-system
route for a bounded set of failure classes. The policy is fail-closed unless
this value is present and valid.

ContentHash.description: SHA-256/Blake3-style content digest represented without exposing secret input.

ContributionKind.description:
Node-local contributions that the owner may veto independently of network
governance. Coordinator participation is deliberately not a local veto:
Coordinator terms are governed by the separate coordinator contract.

oneOf.description: Elected by a majority of the configured candidate group.
Temporary authority during partition. It cannot perform governance writes.

CoordinatorCandidate.description:
One administrator-selected Coordinator candidate. Lower priority values
are preferred, with node identity as the deterministic tie-breaker.

CoordinatorCandidateConfig.description:
Administrator-signed candidate group. Possessing this document is not
sufficient to become Leader: the signer must be a current network manager
when the document is admitted, every candidate must be a network member, and
election still requires the majority protocol defined by `CoordinatorTerm`.

CoordinatorCandidateDeclaration.description:
A short-lived, node-signed statement used as candidate health/eligibility
input. It is never a vote, majority proof or Leader promotion.

CoordinatorCandidateStatus.description:
Shared UI projection. `latest_term` is retained even after expiry so the UI
can show recent tenure without pretending the old leader still has authority.

emergency_leader.description:
Independent bounded runtime-coordination authority used only when every
configured candidate is offline. This is never a normal Leader term and
never enables governance writes.

latest_election.description:
Most recent persisted election, including terminal outcomes. Keeping the
full signed proposal and vote set makes takeover decisions auditable from
the same projection used by clients and operators.

eligible_for_election.description: Eligibility for the election protocol, never an appointment as Leader.

oneOf.description: A full-authority Stable term has a writable lease.
An election is active but has not yet committed a term.

The election ended without a strict majority, or its deadline elapsed
before the durable term could be installed.
The candidate configuration is current, but no term is writable.
The candidate configuration is missing, pending, or expired.
Authority is present but cannot safely perform governance writes.

CoordinatorControlPlaneStatus.description:
Fail-closed projection intended for clients and operators. A missing leader
is not a data-plane failure: `governance_writable = false` only pauses
governance until a strict-majority election installs a fresh term.

CoordinatorElectionProposal.description:
A candidate-signed request to elect one deterministic Leader. A proposal is
not authority: it can only create a persisted election session and the
resulting term is admitted after independently verified strict-majority
votes. The proposer must be the preferred eligible candidate and cannot
appoint another node or itself outside the configured ordering.

CoordinatorElectionSession.description:
Durable election state. Votes are retained for audit and the committed term
is reconstructed from this exact session, preventing a later caller from
substituting a different proof or Leader.

CoordinatorElectionVote.description:
A candidate-signed vote for one exact term and Leader. The signature binds
the network, candidate configuration revision, complete candidate group,
Leader and validity interval so a vote cannot be replayed for another term.

CoordinatorEmergencyLeaderStatus.description:
A bounded, non-governance authority granted only after the Coordinator has
observed every configured candidate offline. The leader is selected
deterministically from online non-candidate members and cannot inherit or
manufacture a normal term.

oneOf.description: No term has been admitted yet. Governance remains in bootstrap mode.
The lease is still writable, but renewal is overdue soon.
Authority is no longer writable until a fresh term is admitted.

CoordinatorLeaseStatus.description:
Observable lease projection used by the control plane and UI. `reason_code`
is stable so a clock-skew alert cannot be mistaken for an ordinary expiry.

CoordinatorPublicReachability.description:
Public reachability evidence supplied by the candidate itself. Consumers
must treat this as a claim until the election protocol verifies a quorum.

CoordinatorWriteCredential.description:
The authority facts that every governance write must carry. The write kind
is supplied separately so one envelope cannot be silently replayed for a
broader operation.

DomainName.description:
Canonical, case-insensitive DNS name used for exact host matching. IDNs are
normalized to their ASCII A-label form and a single trailing root dot is
accepted but not retained.

EffectiveAccessReason.description:
Stable explanation of the final effect. UI surfaces consume this
projection instead of re-implementing rule precedence.

ExitContributionAvailability.description:
Availability projected beside a member's declared capability. Unknown or
stale evidence is never promoted to `available`.

ExitContributionMemberScope.description:
Owner-selected members that may use this node's Exit. The default allows all
active network members; an explicit selection requires at least one subject.

ExitContributionMode.description:
Explicit Exit contribution policy. The legacy obligation/scope pair remains
on the wire for compatibility, but it cannot distinguish voluntary
contribution from a prohibition or an authorization flow. New policies bind
this mode into terms hashes and signed discovery data.

oneOf.description: Members may explicitly opt in; joining never enables Exit locally.
The member must provide Exit capacity as a condition of joining.
Members may not contribute Exit capacity to this network.
Members may request authorization before contributing Exit capacity.

ExitContributionObligation.description:
Exit contribution is an explicit network admission obligation, not a
capability silently enabled by joining.

ExitContributionRestrictions.description:
Owner-authored restrictions beyond the global network allow-list and local
Exit veto. The network allow-list remains `NodeLocalAccessPolicy::network_scope`.

ExitContributionScope.description:
The membership population covered by an Exit contribution obligation.
`NotApplicable` is the only valid scope when contribution is not required.

oneOf.description:
New members accept the obligation when they join. Existing members are
notified but retain their previously acknowledged scope.

Every member must acknowledge the current obligation. This is used for
a policy migration that expands contribution to the existing roster.

ExitContributionTimeWindow.description: UTC half-open minute window. `weekdays` uses Monday=0 through Sunday=6.

ExitHealthEvidence.description:
One sanitized observation. `error_code` is a stable machine token and must
not contain raw command output, addresses or member identity.

ExitHealthRetest.description:
Explicit retest lifecycle. Cancellation is terminal and can never be
rewritten as a successful completion.

ExitHealthTarget.description:
Stable, non-identifying probe targets. A deployment-controlled target may be
named by an opaque ID, but host names, resolver addresses and member
identities are never stored in this health contract.

ExitNodeCapabilities.description:
Current, non-secret Exit Node capability truth for one node process.

`supported` describes whether a basic IPv4 Exit Node can be installed now.
`ipv6_forwarding` is independent because an IPv6-only limitation does not
make the IPv4 Exit Node implementation unusable.

ExitNodePlatform.description: Host platforms with distinct Exit Node implementation requirements.

ExitNodeUnsupportedReason.description:
Machine-readable reasons that make an Exit Node action unavailable.

Adapters must render these reasons instead of treating an enabled config
flag as proof that kernel forwarding and NAT were installed.

ExitSelectionCandidate.description:
Stable reason code and scope for one Exit. Unknown and stale availability is
never reported as selectable.

ExitSelectionGroupRule.description:
An administrator-defined group scope. Membership is part of this policy so
an Exit decision never depends on a client-supplied or stale role label.

ExitSelectionMemberRule.description: A member-specific narrowing or deny. A deny always wins over every allow.

ExitSelectionMode.description:
Schemars cannot infer the human-readable shape from the hand-written serde
implementation above. Keep the JSON contract as the original internally
tagged representation while Postcard uses its own positional-safe form.

ExitSelectionPolicy.description:
Versioned administrator policy. `available_exits` is the network-level
allow set and therefore the universe of all other scopes. Group `allow`
lists narrow that universe when the subject belongs to a matching group;
member `allow` lists narrow it further. Any matching deny removes an Exit
regardless of allow rules at any scope.

ExitSelectionResolution.description:
Complete administrator-authorized set for one subject. Candidate ordering is
stable to make UI and audit output reproducible.

ExitSelectionSource.description: Where the final decision came from.

ExitSessionTransitionPolicy.description:
What to do with an already established session when its Exit is no longer
selectable. `Migrate` may still fail closed if no replacement is available.

FieldPrivacyPolicy.description:
Immutable network-authored field policy. Revisions are monotonic and carry
both issuance and effective time. A malformed, duplicate, expired or
not-yet-effective policy fails closed.

FieldVisibility.description:
Audience ceiling for one field.

The ordering is from least to most restrictive. `serde` aliases preserve
compatibility with the pre-W10 three-level node privacy documents.

FieldVisibilityRule.description: One explicit field override. A policy can only tighten the supplied floor.

InvitationCode.description:
A high-entropy invitation secret. It is intentionally not a URL and its
`Debug` representation is redacted so generic tracing cannot disclose it.

InvitationPreview.description:
Everything the accepting user must see before confirming. It contains no
roster addresses, topology, activity prose or invitation credential.

creates_permanent_membership.description:
Redemption creates ordinary membership and never an invitation-owned or
permanent relationship.

InvitationRecord.description:
Durable invitation metadata. It never contains plaintext invitation code
material; the Coordinator stores only `InvitationCode::digest()` in its
private ledger.

exit_contribution_acknowledged.description:
Explicit consent to the current Exit contribution obligation. It is
required when the invited network requires contribution and is never
inferred from accepting the invitation itself.

already_redeemed.description: True only for an idempotent retry by the same authenticated node.

invited_by.description:
Manager whose active invitation authorized this admission. The
lifecycle ledger revalidates this identity at redemption time.

IpCidr.description:
IP/CIDR matcher stored as text at the contract edge for cross-language
portability and parsed before policy activation.

IssuedInvitation.description:
Safe response from creation. The plaintext code may be displayed/copied once
and is deliberately excluded from list/status responses.

JoinApplicantProfile.description:
Public applicant metadata shown to authorized reviewers. It contains no
private network address, endpoint, activity or credential material.

JoinRequest.description:
Durable approval request. The prose reason is optional solely so retention
cleanup can redact it after the terminal retention deadline; a live pending
request always has a non-empty reason.

approved_at_unix_ms.description:
Exact admission time. `decided_at_unix_ms` is shared by rejection,
withdrawal and expiry and therefore can never be used as join time.

revision.description:
Optimistic concurrency token. A review must supply the revision it was
displayed with so two administrators cannot both approve stale copies.

JoinRequestGrantPreview.description:
Exact authority the member would receive if this request is approved. This
is persisted at submission time so reviewers cannot approve terms different
from those shown in the approval dialog.

JoinRequestReasonVisibility.description:
The only supported visibility for request prose. The reason is deliberately
represented in the durable request record, not in discovery, snapshots,
activities, audit details or event payloads.

LeakDetectionDnsMode.description:
DNS path that was actually observed. DoT support is not implied merely
because this enum can represent it.

LeakDetectionEvidence.description:
One sanitized observation. `error_code` is a stable machine token and must
never contain raw stderr, resolver URLs, addresses or member identity.

LeakDetectionIsolationAction.description:
An isolation action that makes an unsupported path unusable rather than
silently allowing it to leave outside the protected route.

LeakDetectionTarget.description:
Sanitized check target. A controlled service is represented only by its
stable role, never by a host name, URL or resolved address.

LocalExitCapabilitySnapshot.description: Owner intent and observed lifecycle of the local Exit data plane.

MemberLifecycleAction.description:
Every durable governance action uses this vocabulary. Runtime connection
states stay in `MembershipState`; this enum is the operation semantics shared
by the Coordinator, command bus, audit/activity projections and UI adapters.

idempotent.description: True when the response is the durable result of an earlier retry.

MemberLifecycleStatus.description:
Authoritative lifecycle state independent of the local client's connection
workflow. A live data-plane observation may refine `Approved` to `Active`,
but it can never overwrite a suspended, exited or removed tombstone.

MemberRemovalPreview.description:
Explicit, non-secret disclosure shown before removal. It states what will be
revoked without pretending a transfer registry exists where none does.

MembershipRole.description:
A member's governance role. Temporary Coordinator authority is intentionally
represented by `CoordinatorTerm`, never by mutating this durable role.

MembershipState.description: The durable state of one node's relationship with one network.

exit_contribution_mode.description:
Explicit four-mode policy. Omitted from the canonical hash for legacy
Required/JoiningMembers and NotRequired/NotApplicable records so their
acknowledgements and signatures remain verifiable.

member_limit.description:
Capacity shown when these terms were acknowledged. Omitted for legacy
memberships so their content hash remains stable.

NetworkAcl.description:
Revisioned network ACL. Explicit deny rules live in `rules`; direct
role/group/node grants live in `grants` and are subject to expiry,
revocation and reauthentication freshness.

relay_limits.description:
Administrator-authored hard resource bounds for using Relay. Provider
local limits are intersected with these values.

NetworkAclGrant.description:
One explicit direct grant. Grants are additive allow entries; they never
override a matching deny in either authorization layer.

NetworkDiscoveryDocument.description:
Signed discovery data. Endpoints may change between revisions; the stable
network ID remains bound to the immutable network public key.

administrators.description:
Public governance roles disclosed before joining. Full member IDs,
endpoints beyond the signed public hints, topology and activity remain
outside this document.

capability_summary.description:
Canonical capability declaration summary. This is discoverability
metadata, not proof that a capability is currently operational.

language.description:
Public discovery facets. Schema v2 includes these fields in the signed
payload. Defaults keep older local JSON readable while validation still
rejects records created under a different document schema.

publisher.description:
Node that published this revision. Schema v1 binds the publisher to the
network owner so another member cannot publish an owner-authorized card.

revoked_at_unix_ms.description:
A signed tombstone is a normal revision with this timestamp set. Once a
client accepts one, every older or non-identical successor is rejected.

NetworkEndpoint.description: A decoupled discovery hint. It is never part of the stable network identity.

NetworkJoinMode.description: Admission policy selected by the network owner.

oneOf.description: Requests are accepted immediately.
Requests enter `pending_approval`.
The node must first consume a signed, single-use invitation.

NetworkJoinPreview.description:
Short-lived, authenticated disclosure returned by the Coordinator before a
direct network join. It deliberately contains no roster, endpoint topology,
invitation credential or member activity.

signature.description: Signature by the Coordinator/owner identity embedded in the join ticket.

NetworkJoinTerms.description:
Wire-stable membership terms for direct join disclosure. Unlike the legacy
`MembershipTerms` JSON adapter, every field has exactly one binary encoding.

NetworkMember.description:
One sanitized directory row. Fields that are not authorized or not known are
omitted rather than populated from unrelated network-wide declarations.

access_epoch.description: Access generation used to invalidate old credentials and transfers.

available_actions.description:
Actions the authenticated viewer may currently attempt. The server still
re-authorizes and re-checks the transition on mutation.

exit_availability.description:
Authoritative Exit observation for this member. A roster declaration is
not an observation, so missing evidence remains `unknown`.

lifecycle_state.description:
Durable governance state. This is distinct from live connection status
and is always supplied by the lifecycle ledger or an authoritative
roster/request projection.

NetworkMemberDirectory.description:
Server-owned snapshot. A directory never carries endpoints, invitation
material, approval prose, public-key bytes or transfer metadata.

exit_selection_policy.description:
Administrator Exit selection policy for this network. This is part of
the authenticated member projection rather than the public discovery
document so member and group rules are only exposed to network members.

exit_selection_policy_revision.description:
Revision of the network policy carried with the directory. Consumers
must reject older revisions instead of replacing fresher governance.

viewer_role.description: Role observed from the authoritative roster, never from a client claim.

NetworkMemberGroup.description:
Current system groups. Custom and dynamic groups are introduced separately;
role-derived groups here are never inferred from a client-owned label.

NetworkMemberObservationSource.description:
Why presence has its current value. The timestamp lets both UIs display the
observation's freshness without inventing a client-side observation.

NetworkMemberOnlineState.description:
Three-state presence. Unknown means the Coordinator has never observed the
member's data-plane session and must never be presented as offline.

NetworkMemberStatus.description:
Authoritative, sanitized member status shown by governance surfaces.

This is deliberately distinct from [`MembershipState`], which tracks the
local node's connection workflow. In particular, an approved roster member
is not reported as active until a live data-plane session observes it.

oneOf.description: 仅使用 IPv4 虚拟内网
仅使用 IPv6 虚拟内网
同时支持 IPv4 和 IPv6 虚拟双栈

NetworkProfileUpdate.description:
Owner-editable public fields for an existing network. The network name and
stable identity deliberately cannot be changed through this command.

NetworkPublicProfileDocument.description:
Public profile data that is safe to show before membership. This type is
an allowlist: it has no member identities, assigned addresses, endpoints,
topology, activity history or secret references.

NetworkPublicProfileProjection.description:
Exact public-card projection plus the categories that are withheld. The
withheld values themselves never cross this boundary.

NetworkRole.description: Durable network roles plus the runtime-only emergency Coordinator role.

NetworkVisibility.description: How much of a network's public profile is discoverable without membership.

NodeAccessControlSnapshot.description:
Trusted authorization documents carried with the authoritative node state.
`local_policy` is authored by the node owner; each network ACL is authored by
that network's governance. Duplicate network ACLs are never resolved by
ordering and cause command authorization to fail closed.

field_privacy_policies.description:
Versioned network-authored field disclosure documents. Like ACLs,
these are trusted control-plane data and never come from command JSON.

NodeAcknowledgeMembershipPolicyCommand.description:
Re-confirm the exact signed network terms after a policy migration that
covers existing members. The hash pins the disclosure the owner saw; the
separate Exit flag can never be inferred from accepting the terms.

NodeApiErrorResponse.description:
Versioned error response. The `problem` payload is optional because some
transport-level failures do not originate from a node command.

NodeApiEvent.description:
JSON payload carried by `/api/v1/events` Server-Sent Events. The stream
begins with a canonical snapshot and then carries ordered node events.

cursor.description:
Resume position for this connection. The snapshot itself is already
authoritative; replayed events after this cursor are notifications
that the client may deduplicate by sequence.

NodeApiObject.description:
A single canonical object fetched by kind and ID. Objects are projections of
the authoritative snapshot, never independently maintained UI state.

NodeApiOperationResponse.description: Versioned response for operation submission and lookup.

confirm_privilege_expansion.description: Explicit acknowledgement of the high-risk privilege-expansion summary.

confirm_risk.description:
Explicit acknowledgement of any high-risk fixed Exit, broad matcher or
fail-open consequence shown in preview.

changed.description:
True when the operation changed persisted blacklist state. Queries and
idempotent mutations report false.

NodeCapabilityRegistrySnapshot.description:
Stable projection of the fixed first-version capability set. Unknown
entries fail closed and unsupported capabilities remain visible so the UI
can explain why an action is unavailable.

NodeCleanupStepSnapshot.description:
One sanitized runtime cleanup step. Host paths and raw operating-system
errors are intentionally excluded from this public contract.

NodeCommand.description:
Product-neutral node operations. A node creates, joins or serves a network;
there are deliberately no product-level client/server command variants.

oneOf.description:
Bootstrap query for the declarative UI contract. This is not rendered as
a page action and should be called before an adapter builds its UI.

Query live runtime residue and cleanup state from the actor that owns
network sessions, embedded services and retained resource owners.
Recreate one network's TUN under the actor-owned lifecycle transition.
Build the exact public-card preview and field-level diff without writing.
Atomically apply, re-sign and audit a public profile update.
Sign and publish the current public profile to a discovery index.
Sign a newer discovery revision and publish it.
Sign and publish a terminal revocation for a discovery record.
Fetch and verify the signed discovery index without changing any data plane.
Retry the last configured discovery index after an outage.
Read-only disclosure preview for a signed open-network discovery record.

Confirm and directly join a network using signed discovery material that
is revalidated against the persisted revision/revocation watermark.
Submit an owner-authored request to join an approval-required network.

List the caller's own requests or every request when the caller is a
current network owner/administrator.
Read the Coordinator-authoritative, privacy-filtered member directory.
Disclose the exact access, File and data impact before member removal.
Apply one revision-checked member lifecycle governance action.
Apply one revision-checked approval decision.
Apply a revision-checked approval batch atomically.
Withdraw the caller's own pending request.
Answer an information request and return it to pending review.
Create a one-time authenticated invitation and reveal its credential once.
List redacted invitation metadata for one managed network.
Read one invitation's redacted status.
Revoke an invitation using its current revision.
Preview an invitation before local-owner reauthentication and consent.
Consume an invitation and create ordinary network membership.
Remove only this network's local configuration and membership.
Re-confirm the exact latest terms after an `AllMembers` policy change.

Owner-controlled local intent for actually serving as an Exit Node.
Network authorization remains in each network's `exit_node.enabled`.

Start all persistently configured networks while keeping this node IPC
and the control/UI processes alive.

Stop all data-plane sessions and owned embedded services while keeping
this node IPC and the control/UI processes alive.

Reload every persisted network and replace the complete data plane under
one single-flight lifecycle operation.

Retry cleanup for runtime resources whose previous owner reported a
deferred or failed shutdown.
Complete redacted configuration for every configured network.
Validate an imported complete configuration without writing it.
Persist all network configurations under one revision transaction.
Restore a previous revision as a new auditable revision.
Append-only configuration revision history, newest first.
Current authoritative policy revision and normalized policy snapshot.
Compute a policy diff and risk summary without writing it.
Compute the diff and risk for restoring a previous revision without writing it.
Atomically replace the complete policy snapshot under one revision.
Restore a previous policy generation as a new auditable revision.
Append-only policy revision history, newest first.

Evaluate candidate policy documents with the runtime authorization evaluator
without storing them or emitting audit/activity side effects.
Current authoritative traffic-routing policy revision.
Compute a traffic-routing diff and risk summary without writing it.
Compute the diff for restoring a previous traffic policy revision.
Atomically install and verify a complete traffic policy.
Restore a previous traffic policy generation as a new revision.
Append-only traffic policy revision history, newest first.

Compare a current and candidate traffic policy for one hypothetical flow
without touching host networking, persistence, audit or activity.
Read the authoritative Coordinator candidate health projection.
Replace the administrator-signed candidate group using optimistic revision.

Publish this node's signed health/willingness declaration; `Unwilling`
is the owner's explicit refusal of the local candidate role.

NodeCommandHttpRequest.description:
Versioned request DTO for `POST /api/node/commands`.

The embedded `NodeCommandRequest` is forwarded unchanged to
`NodeCommandBus`; the adapter does not inspect or mutate node state.

idempotency_key.description:
Required for mutating commands. Reusing the key with the same command
returns the original operation; reusing it with another command is a
conflict and never dispatches a second side effect.

NodeCommandHttpResponse.description:
Versioned response DTO containing the exact result returned by the command
bus. Rejected results remain visible in the body alongside their HTTP status.

NodeCommandRequest.description: One request accepted by the node command layer from CLI, IPC, WebUI or GPUI.

NodeConfigurationSnapshot.description: Effective, non-secret network configuration exposed to every UI adapter.

NodeContributionVeto.description: A non-overridable local contribution veto for one network.

NodeControlHealth.description: Whether the adapter can currently reach the node control plane.

expires_in_ms.description:
Requested lifetime in milliseconds. The domain bounds this to one minute
through thirty days.

exit_selection_policy.description:
Administrator-owned Exit selection governance. Legacy payloads default
to member choice with no additional network/group/member narrowing.

NodeCreatedNetwork.description:
Owner-local result of creating a network.

The invitation ticket is deliberately returned only by this command result
and is never added to `NodeSnapshot`, events, or logs. Its `Debug` output is
redacted so an adapter cannot accidentally leak it through generic error
formatting.

NodeDiagnosticCheck.description:
One sanitized layered probe. Raw process output, host paths, interface MAC
addresses, tokens, keys, full topology and peer addresses are excluded.

error_code.description: Stable machine code, never raw stderr.

NodeDiagnosticLayer.description: Stable diagnostic layers shown in a fixed order by every adapter.

NodeDiagnosticRecoveryAction.description:
A recovery action that is safe to render from untrusted UI input. The UI
must request explicit confirmation when `confirmation_required` is true and
show the impact key before dispatching any command.

NodeDiagnosticState.description:
Five-state result deliberately richer than a boolean. Adapters must render
every state verbatim and must not infer `passed` from missing probe data.

NodeDiagnosticsSnapshot.description: Live actor-owned diagnostics plus a bounded layered probe report.

exit_health.description:
Layered local Exit evidence. Missing/stale DNS or Internet evidence is
visible here and cannot be promoted from the process state.

exit_health_assessment.description:
Server-authoritative assessment at `completed_at_unix_ms`. Clients render
this result and never recompute health from process state.

leak_detection.description:
Bounded local DNS, IPv4 and IPv6 evidence. Missing, stale, unsupported or
unexecuted checks remain visible and are never promoted to a pass.

sanitized_report.description:
Canonical redacted report suitable for clipboard/export. It is generated
server-side from stable fields, never from raw stderr.

NodeDiscoveryIndexErrorCategory.description: Stable, non-secret categories for persisted request failures.

NodeDiscoveryIndexMetrics.description:
Aggregate-only discovery telemetry. It deliberately has no URL, response
body, search text, record name or free-form error text.

NodeDiscoveryIndexSnapshot.description: Public discovery-index status included in the canonical node snapshot.

data_plane_affected.description:
The discovery index is a control-plane convenience. Its state never
changes any joined network's lifecycle or forwarding data plane.

search_history_stored.description:
The discovery index client has no search-query field. This explicit flag
documents the privacy contract for generated UI and Android clients.

NodeDiscoveryIndexSource.description:
One signed record accepted from the index or supplied by a join flow.

`discoverable` is false for expired, malformed or revoked records. The raw
signed record is retained so revocations and revision watermarks survive a
restart and can reject later rollback attempts.

NodeDiscoveryIndexState.description: Stable discovery-index states consumed by every UI adapter.

NodeErrorCategory.description:
Stable error domains shared by command results, HTTP responses and
WebSocket failures. UI code must branch on this category rather than parse
human-readable messages.

NodeEventCursor.description:
Point in the node event stream. Sequence provides exactly-once delivery
within retained history; snapshot revision proves the cursor belongs to the
snapshot epoch the consumer is applying.

NodeExitSelectionSnapshot.description:
One network's administrator-owned Exit selection policy plus the exact
deny-first resolution produced by the trusted runtime. Older snapshots omit
this field and therefore must not infer an authorized Exit.

NodeHttpErrorCode.description: Stable error codes for HTTP version negotiation and backend failures.

NodeHttpErrorResponse.description:
Versioned HTTP error DTO. It is also used for WebSocket version mismatches
so clients receive a machine-readable failure before an upgrade.

NodeIdentityRotationSnapshot.description:
Public result of a completed node key rotation. The DTO deliberately
contains fingerprints and identifiers only; private keys and owner tokens
never cross the command boundary.

NodeInterfaceOwnership.description:
Product ownership is established by an exact match against the live
runtime's TUN name. Interface naming conventions never establish ownership.

discovery_record.description:
Public signed discovery material selected by the user. It is never
trusted as cached authority: the handler replaces or revalidates it from
the persisted discovery snapshot immediately before mutation.

exit_contribution_acknowledged.description:
Explicit acknowledgement of the network's Exit contribution obligation.
A network declaration never enables this node's local Exit service.

network_id.description: Stable network selected from a discovery preview.

preview_digest.description: Exact discovery digest shown in the preview.

signed_join_preview.description:
Signed, short-lived disclosure obtained from the Coordinator before a
direct ticket join. The handler revalidates it against the ticket and
uses it as the consent record that authorizes membership persistence.

requests.description:
Reviewer callers receive every network request; other callers receive
only their own requests. Reason and notes remain private fields.

NodeLifecycleSnapshot.description: Shared lifecycle snapshot consumed by CLI, IPC, WebUI, and (later) GPUI.

NodeLocalAccessPolicy.description:
The trusted, owner-authored local authorization layer. A network
administrator can add further restrictions but can never replace this
document or any of its vetoes.

exit_contribution.description: Owner restrictions specific to serving as an Exit for a network.

relay_limits.description:
Owner-authored hard resource bounds for serving Relay on this node.
Network ACL limits are intersected with these values; this document can
make them stricter but cannot loosen network-authored bounds.

NodeManifestResponse.description: Versioned DTO returned by the UI-manifest endpoint.

NodeNetworkAllocation.description:
Transport-neutral allocation payload shared by local adapters and the
node command protocol. Persistence is owned by the embedded service actor,
never by a UI adapter.

NodeNetworkConfigSnapshot.description:
One network's effective configuration after loading startup overrides.

Filesystem paths and other host-local details are deliberately omitted. The
boolean fields only state whether optional host-local settings are present.

can_join_without_local_exit.description: True only when a member can join without promising Exit contribution.

exit_contribution_purpose_key.description:
Stable disclosure keys cover what the local owner is consenting to.
They never enable or advertise the local Exit service by themselves.

join_requires_exit_consent.description: The direct join confirmation must explicitly acknowledge this obligation.

local_exit_available.description: Local host support is separate from the network's declaration.

local_exit_enabled.description: This is the node's actual local role state, never inferred from terms.

locally_contributed_capabilities.description:
Capabilities remain locally controlled. The only admission obligation
is disclosed separately as Exit contribution.

preview_digest.description:
The digest also binds discovery revision, policy disclosures, endpoints,
capability declarations and expiry.

terms_hash.description: Current join terms are hashed exactly as acknowledged by the owner.

NodeNetworkMembershipSnapshot.description:
Public, owner-editable network metadata rendered by every UI adapter.

This is deliberately a separate projection from `NetworkRecord`: secrets,
members, addresses, topology, activity and invitations are not fields and
therefore cannot be serialized by accident.

current_terms.description:
Signed terms most recently observed from discovery. When these differ
from `terms_hash`, members see a policy-change notice; the separate
boolean distinguishes notice-only metadata changes from Exit disclosure
or privacy changes that require explicit acknowledgement.

NodeNetworkRole.description: Network roles are capabilities within a network, never product identities.

NodeNetworkScope.description:
A node owner can either participate in every authenticated network or
explicitly limit participation to a fixed set. An empty `Only` set is
invalid rather than an accidental allow-all sentinel.

NodeNetworkSelection.description: How a node should choose the networks it loads at startup.

oneOf.description: Keep the node and its control surfaces running without joining a network.

NodeOperationSnapshot.description:
Transport projection of the shared `Operation` state machine. `result` is
only populated after a mutation reaches a terminal state; consumers must
treat a queued/running operation as in progress, never as successful.

attempt.description:
The number of execution attempts started. A retry uses the same
operation id and idempotency key but starts a new attempt.

cancel_blocked_reason.description:
Stable localization key explaining why cancellation is unavailable.
Terminal operations may omit it because there is no action to explain.

cancellable.description:
Whether this operation may be cancelled without guessing from its kind
or current stage. Transport adapters must project this value verbatim.

NodePermission.description: Stable capability classes used by both the permission snapshot and UI actions.

NodePermissionSnapshot.description:
Control-plane authorization posture shared with UI adapters.

`TrustedControlPlane` means the runtime accepts every connected adapter as
fully privileged. It does not mean per-user or remote authentication exists.

NodePhase.description:
Node-global lifecycle. Network sessions may come and go while the node
remains in one of these phases.

NodePreviewConfigurationCommand.description:
Complete document imported by an owner for preview or atomic apply.
Actor and request source are intentionally absent: the command bus supplies
them from the authenticated transport context.

coordinator_url.description:
Coordinator endpoint is a separate routing hint, never part of the
invitation credential and never placed in the URL query.

NodePreviewPolicyCommand.description:
A complete normalized policy snapshot. The server computes the actual
affected scope so the caller can review it before supplying the scope to an
apply command.

NodePreviewTrafficPolicyCommand.description:
Editable traffic-routing document. Runtime state, effect plans and
authorization identity remain server-owned.

NodeProblem.description: UI- and transport-neutral error returned by every node command adapter.

oneOf.description:
A finite host resource (memory, file descriptors, storage or firewall
capacity) prevented the requested operation.
The operation is valid but unavailable on this platform or host.

NodeProblemDetails.description:
Stable machine-readable error details. Human-readable messages remain in
`NodeProblem::message`, while these fields are safe for adapters to use for
field highlighting and revision conflict recovery.

validity_ms.description: Short declaration lease. Runtime signs the exact timestamps.

coordinator_url.description:
Coordinator endpoint is a separate routing hint, never part of the
invitation credential and never placed in the URL query.

NodeResidualCleanupResult.description: Partial-success aware result for explicit residual cleanup.

expected_fingerprint.description:
The current public-key fingerprint shown to the owner. Requiring it
prevents a stale UI from rotating a newer identity that it has not seen.

NodeRoutingDefaultAction.description:
The default action currently applied to traffic that does not match a
network-specific rule.

NodeRoutingSummarySnapshot.description:
One network's authoritative traffic-policy state as last applied by the
node runtime. Editable configuration remains in `NodeConfigurationSnapshot`.

oneOf.description: Runtime accepted the policy and the matching snapshot was published.

The last successful application predates the current stopped/runtime
state and must not be treated as active.
Policy validation rejected the configuration before mutation.
The runtime or snapshot publication failed after an application attempt.

NodeRoutingTargetSnapshot.description: Concrete traffic path behind a network or Exit default action.

NodeRuntimeResidueSnapshot.description: Transport-neutral residue report shared by diagnostics and explicit cleanup.

NodeSetLocalExitCapabilityCommand.description:
Node-owner intent for the local Exit data plane.

This does not grant network exposure. A live network also has to carry the
Exit Node role in its network configuration. Disabling this value is a local
veto that network administrators cannot override.

NodeSnapshotResponse.description: Versioned DTO returned by the snapshot endpoint.

audit.description:
Stable audit requirement for this command. Reads that are too noisy to
record still carry an explicit `none` declaration instead of leaving
adapters to guess.

NodeUiActionBlockReason.description:
Canonical reasons that can disable a manifest action. The enum is flat so
WebUI, GPUI, generated bindings and Android consume the same fail-closed
vocabulary even when their local capability snapshots have richer details.

action.description: Stable action name written to the append-only audit log.

oneOf.description: The production command handler currently accepts this command.
The shared command exists, but the runtime backend rejects it as unavailable.

consequence_key.description: Human-readable scope and impact shown before submission.

NodeUiManifest.description:
Declarative contract shared by WebUI and the future native GPUI surface.

Adapters may choose different widgets and rendering, but page availability,
commands, fields, validation, confirmations, permission classes and backend
maturity come from this manifest rather than duplicated UI business logic.

NodeUiPageState.description: Canonical node-page states shared by every UI adapter.

credential.description:
Present after the first authoritative term is installed. Bootstrap
updates before a term are deliberately credential-free and are rejected
by the Coordinator once a term exists.

NodeValidationIssue.description: Structured field-level validation issue carried by a command error.

NodeWsMessage.description:
Versioned WebSocket messages. A snapshot is sent immediately after upgrade;
every later state or operational event carries the same adapter version.

oneOf.description:
Transport-neutral error metadata carried by HTTP, WebSocket and operation
failures. `message` remains a human-readable fallback; clients branch on
`code`, `category` and `message_key`, interpolate `params`, and use
`recovery` to offer a safe next action.

NodeWsResyncReason.description: Why the server replaced the event stream with a fresh canonical snapshot.

oneOf.description: The broadcast receiver fell behind and lost one or more events.
Event revisions skipped values, so incremental application is unsafe.

partial_changes.description: Cancellation is not the same as having no side effects.

PermissionIntent.description:
Whether a request can mutate durable state. Temporary Coordinators may read
the last valid policy and coordinate existing connections, but every
mutating request is frozen in the domain evaluator.

path.description: Stable JSON Pointer rooted at the policy snapshot.

PolicyPrecedence.description:
Fixed precedence order consumed by the UI. The evaluator remains the sole
authority for the selected outcome; this trace only explains which gate was
active and in what order gates were considered.

applied.description:
Whether this rule/factor could contribute to the evaluated decision.
Revoked, expired and stale-reauthentication grants are matched but not
applied.

matched.description: Whether this rule/factor matched the submitted request context.

precedence.description: The precedence label associated with this rule or factor.

PolicyRuleSource.description:
Stable source labels. They identify where a rule or factor came from
without changing the evaluator's final decision.

PolicySnapshot.description:
Complete policy documents governed by one optimistic transaction. Network
ACLs are normalized by stable network ID and never by caller-selected order.

PolicyTestInput.description:
Complete, transport-safe input for a policy test. Candidate documents are
evaluated in memory and are never applied to the node.

decision.description:
Final outcome and all matched identifiers from the authoritative runtime
evaluator. Consumers must display these fields as-is.

path.description: JSON-pointer-style path into the submitted policy document.

PrivacyField.description:
Stable field identifiers. Serialized policies and public previews use these
names verbatim; hidden values are never represented by a masked placeholder.

ProjectedActivityEntry.description:
Activity projection. Required identity/timeline fields remove the whole
entry when hidden; optional prose fields are omitted from JSON entirely.

ProjectedNetworkMemberDirectory.description:
A member directory that has already passed field projection. The inner
canonical value is intentionally private so adapters cannot accidentally
serialize an unprojected directory through this DTO.

ProjectedNodeCommandResult.description:
Wire-safe command result. Sensitive variants carry projected DTOs rather
than canonical snapshots or member directories.

relay_authorization.description:
Sanitized authorization layers are owner-only. They explain the final
decision without exposing rules, grants or another member's traffic.

relay_governance.description:
Payload-free governance events are owner-only. Ordinary members never
receive the ledger, including rejection reason codes that could reveal
another member's activity.

relay_health.description:
Relay listener, limits, usage and failure details are owner-visible.
Ordinary members receive only the non-sensitive lifecycle projection.

ProjectedNodeEvent.description:
Event with field-level projection applied. Log contents are omitted for
non-owner viewers while the sequence and snapshot revision remain intact so
cursors still advance without silently skipping an event.

ProjectedNodeSnapshot.description:
A node snapshot whose sensitive fields have already been removed. Optional
hidden values are serialized by omission; arrays that would only contain
hidden rows are omitted as well.

traffic_session.description:
Authoritative local protection state. It contains only stable state,
timestamps, reason codes and validation booleans, so every authorized
snapshot viewer can render it without receiving host details.

PublicKey.description: Ed25519 public key bytes encoded as URL-safe base64 without padding.

RelayAuthorizationAuditSnapshot.description:
Bounded, deterministic snapshot of current Relay member decisions. The
owner sees which authorization layer produced the final result without the
matching rule/grant identifiers or any connection metadata.

truncated.description: True when the policy contained more members than the bounded projection.

RelayAuthorizationSourceDiagnostic.description:
Sanitized authorization evidence for the Relay owner. It deliberately omits
rule and grant identifiers, matched subjects and transport metadata while
retaining the layer, reason and revisions needed to explain both sides of
the final decision.

RelayExistingSessionPolicy.description: How existing sessions react when Relay authorization changes.

oneOf.description: Keep the already-established encrypted QUIC session until it closes.

Move the member to another authorized Relay without dropping its P2P
overlay session.
Close the relayed session promptly and fail closed.

RelayGovernanceAction.description: Stable governance action names for audit records and activity filters.

RelayGovernanceAuditSnapshot.description:
Snapshot returned by the Relay governance sink. Older events are evicted
first; `dropped_events` makes queue pressure observable rather than silent.

RelayGovernanceEvent.description:
One bounded, payload-free Relay governance observation.

Events intentionally carry no source/destination address, peer display
name, packet payload, key material or session secret. `node_id` identifies
the consumer whose request was rejected or whose authorization changed so
an owner can filter the audit without exposing the Relay topology.

policy_revision.description: Policy revision that became effective for this governance event.

previous_policy_revision.description: Policy revision observed before an authorization or quota update.

RelayHealthSnapshot.description:
Health is derived from observed state. It cannot be set to healthy by a UI
merely because an owner intent or capability declaration is present.

RelayLimitPolicy.description:
Hard limit set for one Relay direction. When a network policy and a node
policy both define a value, [`RelayLimitPolicy::intersection`] keeps the
stricter one.

RelayUsageSnapshot.description:
Measured Relay work. This is a projection, not an accounting journal; the
authoritative audit remains the append-only audit chain.

Signature.description: Signature bytes encoded as URL-safe base64 without padding.

TopologyBoundary.description:
One network boundary. `member_count` is the authoritative count, while
`visible_member_count` reflects aggregation so a surface can explain it.

TopologyCluster.description: Aggregated remainder of an oversized network.

TopologyConnection.description: One unordered node pair, with every network that observed it.

TopologyConnectionState.description:
Link state as observed, not as assumed. `Stale` is terminal for rendering
purposes: it never counts as an active link.

TopologyNode.description: Exactly one entry per `NodeId`, regardless of how many networks it joins.

networks.description: Sorted by network id so both UIs render the same order.

TopologyNodeHealth.description:
Aggregated node health. `Unknown` is deliberately distinct from `Healthy`
so a surface can never claim a healthy node it has not observed.

TopologyNodeNetwork.description: The node's relationship with one visible network.

TrafficAction.description:
Exactly one traffic decision. Network and Exit decisions carry the concrete
target in the variant, so a rule can never return an ambiguous set of exits.

TrafficDefaultConfirmedBy.description:
Who explicitly confirmed the fallback decision for traffic that matches no
rule. There is intentionally no default confirmation value.

TrafficDefaultPolicy.description:
A visible, acknowledged fallback. Runtime evaluation must never infer a
fallback from a mode, recommendation, or absent rule.

direct_fallback.description: Present only for an explicitly confirmed direct fallback.

TrafficFailureKind.description: A condition that prevents the selected route from being used.

oneOf.description: Process identity could not be established for an application condition.
DNS resolution did not produce an answer before the deadline.
DNS answers failed authenticity/consistency checks and may be poisoned.
The selected network or concrete Exit is no longer available.
No authorized network path could be selected.
A connection did not establish before the policy deadline.

The secure handshake with a Relay or Exit was interrupted after it
started. Existing flows may have observed partial authentication state,
so this class must fail closed.

The local runtime lost ownership of or disconnected from the data-plane
process. It cannot prove that traffic remained inside the protected
path, so this class must fail closed.

Some attempts completed and others failed, so switching routes would be
ambiguous or could leak an already-established flow.

direct_fallback.description: Absence is the fail-closed default and is not shown as confirmation.

destination_cidrs.description:
Exact IP values are canonicalized as `/32` or `/128`; CIDRs are matched
only against the observed destination IP.

domain_suffixes.description:
Complete-label DNS suffix match, for example `example.com` also matches
`www.example.com` but never `notexample.com` or `example.com.evil`.

exact_domains.description:
Exact, normalized DNS names. This condition never parses or compares IP
literals and never matches a subdomain.

TrafficMatchRisk.description:
A non-blocking warning attached to a matcher. Invalid or ambiguous values
are rejected by `validate`; these codes describe valid rules whose scope is
intentionally or accidentally broad and must be shown before activation.

failure_policy.description:
Failure handling is part of the policy revision, not an ambient mode.
Missing values deserialize to the fail-closed default.

path.description: Stable JSON Pointer rooted at the applied policy content.

TrafficPolicyDraft.description:
Editable traffic policy content. A draft deliberately has no revision:
preview computes the successor and apply records the revision only after
all runtime effects have been verified.

TrafficPolicyTestContextSource.description:
Where the prefilled test context came from. Activity and diagnostic
identifiers are stable object references, allowing the UI to implement
one-click prefill without copying localized display text into the contract.

TrafficPolicyTestDecision.description:
A serialization-safe result projection. The route-summary variant physically
omits hidden details instead of relying on frontend masking.

failure_outcomes_changed.description: Hidden in the route-summary projection for the same reason.

matched_rule_changed.description:
Hidden in the route-summary projection because it would reveal whether
the same private rule matched before and after the edit.

TrafficPolicyTestInput.description:
Complete input for a side-effect-free traffic policy test. `network_id` is
the network membership context in which the hypothetical flow occurs;
`fixed_exit` and `fixed_network` model administrator-visible hard routing
constraints that direct fallback must never bypass.

TrafficProtectionState.description: What the runtime can prove about the local traffic path right now.

oneOf.description: No protected route has been selected yet.
A route is being established and has not completed validation.

An existing route is being replaced and traffic is fail-closed until
the replacement completes validation.
Fresh TUN, route, DNS and reachability evidence all passed.
Traffic must be stopped because the selected route cannot be trusted.

The owner/administrator explicitly allowed this exact failure class to
use the operating-system route.

TrafficRoutingHardConstraints.description:
Hard routing constraints shown alongside the policy. They are not editable
policy rules and must never be bypassed by direct fallback.

TrafficRoutingMoveAction.description:
One equivalent pointer/keyboard/button action. Adapters bind drag-and-drop
and keyboard gestures to the same action ID rather than implementing a
second ordering path.

TrafficRoutingObservation.description:
A bounded observation window produced by the real traffic data plane. Only
samples that the runtime actually observed are present here; adapters must
never synthesize hits from tests, fixtures or configuration.

observed_flow_count.description:
Total observed flows in the window, including flows outside the
bounded sample list.

TrafficRoutingObservedHit.description:
One real observed flow that matched the rule. `activity_id` or
`diagnostic_id` provides the stable one-click source for the tester.

authority_revision.description: Applied authority revision, not a local form counter.

can_edit.description:
Whether the current caller may create a draft or apply it. Read-only
callers still receive the authoritative page and target navigation.

observation.description:
Observation availability is part of the authoritative page so the UI
can distinguish an observed zero-hit window from missing data.

TrafficRoutingRuleActivityEffect.description:
The observable consequence of disabling or deleting a rule. `NoObservedTraffic`
means an available observation window confirmed zero matching flows; it is
never used when the observation source is unavailable.

delete_impact.description: Authoritative consequence of deleting this rule.

disable_impact.description:
Authoritative consequence of disabling this rule. The default keeps old
snapshots honest: absence of observation data is unavailable, not zero
hits.

TrafficRoutingTarget.description:
A navigable reference to a routing target. Labels are display hints; stable
IDs and `navigation` are the authority used by every adapter.

TrafficRoutingWorkflowState.description:
The editor workflow state. `Draft`, `Applying`, `Applied`, `Failed` and
`Stale` are intentionally separate so an adapter cannot infer success from
an editable document or from the mere presence of a revision.

oneOf.description: No authoritative traffic policy has been loaded yet.

TrafficSessionEvent.description:
A compact, transport-neutral activity record. It contains stable state and
reason codes only; Exit identities, addresses, resolver URLs and command
output stay outside this projection.

TrafficSessionSnapshot.description: The single source of truth consumed by GPUI, WebUI and protocol adapters.

TrafficSessionValidation.description: Evidence required before the session may become `Protected`.

TunCapabilities.description:
Redacted TUN readiness for the current node process. This is deliberately
derived from capability metadata rather than a real TUN creation probe.

UiMode.description:
The actual control surface selected for this node process.

`WebUi` is the browser-hosted control plane for headless hosts. A process
with a desktop session must use `Gpui`; it must not expose the WebUI as a
second desktop surface.

description:
Schema-only envelope for the complete HTTP/WebSocket surface. It is never
serialized on the wire; it exists so one root schema can reference every
versioned HTTP DTO from the same Rust definitions used at runtime.
title: NodeHttpContract
